disposition_reason: Resolve Engineering Decision Pending and BLOCKED without changing the Master. NVIDIA's NVDEC guide explicitly defines MPEG-1 hardware decode, decoded YUV output and a separate rendering path. FFmpeg supplies probe/decode and frame-signature mechanisms. The test can therefore be written with authoritative semantics now: require an immutable known-good MPEG-1 input and golden decoded-frame manifest as runtime configuration, bind the exact supported decoder/GPU, reject fallback, verify every expected frame/timestamp, then retain real connector-bound visual evidence for the original display coverage. Missing file paths, GPU selectors and approved golden values are prerequisites, not unresolved engineering semantics.
decision_basis: The exact XLSX row 1784, same-row DeepSeek/test-json content, GPT V2, historical V3.1 record, Round-2 UNRESOLVED result, pending/blocked analyses, ED-01 through ED-30 and official NVIDIA/FFmpeg documentation were read. The next formal identity was directly opened as Functionality row 1785 / Wistron-HW-00418-V002 / 908b15334c705614.

Items and Procedure are coherent: decode produces video frames and Procedure requires displaying those frames. There is no Master source conflict; DeepSeek's encoder substitution is a review-layer error and is discarded.

NVIDIA documents MPEG-1 as an NVDEC codec, requires querying decoder capability, and describes decoded YUV frames plus the additional graphics steps required to present them. This supplies the technical stage boundary without inventing OEM behavior.

An immutable project-approved MPEG-1 stream, its expected metadata and a golden frame-signature manifest can be runtime configuration. Exact GPU UUID/BDF, driver, decoder API, output format, connector and evidence path are likewise bindable parameters with fail-closed validation.

PASS can be objective for decode: input hash and metadata match, the selected hardware path is proven with no fallback, decoded frame count/timestamps and per-frame signatures match the golden reference, the command exits cleanly and health/events remain acceptable.

The original visual coverage is not replaced by hashes. A qualified operator must observe the complete connector-bound playback and record no corruption, tearing, frozen/missing frames, unintended crop/border or edge artifacts against the approved reference.

The 1-minute Machine Time is scheduling metadata, not an approved clip duration. Runtime must use the complete approved clip or explicitly configured frame range and never truncate it to fit the estimate.
No MPEG-1 encode/decode, GPU workload, scratch write, playback, display inspection, log clear or DUT action was executed.

test_case.test_name: MPEG-1 hardware decode integrity and connector-bound display
test_case.purpose: Validate the approved MPEG-1 bitstream is decoded through the bound hardware path with exact frame integrity and is displayed completely on the approved physical output without visual defects, preserving both machine-verifiable decode and human visual coverage.
required_package: Project configuration: immutable known-good MPEG-1 stream, SHA-256, container/profile/resolution/frame-rate/duration/expected frame and timestamp values, golden decoded `framemd5` manifest and its specified output pixel format
Exact GPU serial/UUID/BDF and OS device selector; driver/VBIOS plus an ffmpeg/ffprobe build with the approved NVDEC-capable hardware-acceleration path and verbose no-fallback evidence
Approved bounded scratch and evidence directories with preflight capacity greater than configured decoded/log output; do not use production-data paths
Approved physical connector/display/mode/player/capture route and qualified visual operator; baseline/final GPU, thermal/power, driver/Xid, OS and BMC event collectors
Approved abort thresholds and non-destructive media/GPU/display recovery plan
test_case.test_command: PARAMETERIZED REVIEW-LAYER PROCEDURE — do not execute until all variables are approved. (1) Verify the configured input SHA-256 and golden-manifest SHA-256, scratch containment/capacity, exact GPU identity and healthy baseline; preserve existing logs rather than clearing them. (2) Record `ffprobe -v error -show_streams -show_format -of json "$MPEG1_INPUT"` and require exact configured codec/container/profile/resolution/rate/duration metadata. (3) Record ffmpeg build, hardware accelerators/decoders and device capability. Run `ffmpeg -hide_banner -loglevel repeat+level+verbose -hwaccel "$APPROVED_HWACCEL" -hwaccel_device "$GPU_SELECTOR" -i "$MPEG1_INPUT" -map 0:v:0 -an -vf "$APPROVED_HW_DOWNLOAD_AND_PIXEL_FORMAT" -f framemd5 "$ACTUAL_FRAMEMD5"`; the instantiated filter/pixel format must equal the golden contract. (4) Fail closed unless logs prove the bound hardware decoder with no software fallback; compare complete frame count, timestamps and `framemd5` output byte-for-byte with the approved golden manifest. (5) Play the same complete immutable input through the approved hardware decode/display route on the bound connector; the qualified operator records time-correlated visual evidence from first through last frame. (6) Collect final health/events and exit codes. Stop on any mismatch or anomaly; preserve evidence and do not retry.
test_case.expected_result: The input and golden hashes/metadata match configuration; the exact bound hardware decoder is selected with no fallback; all configured frames and timestamps decode and every frame signature matches the golden manifest in the specified pixel format; ffmpeg completes once with exit code 0 and no decode errors. Complete connector-bound playback shows no corrupted/missing/frozen frames, tearing, unintended crop/border or edge artifact, and final GPU/system health and event deltas remain within approved limits.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS only when every automated integrity condition and the complete qualified visual observation pass, with immutable evidence. FAIL on wrong/unapproved input, metadata/hash mismatch, unsupported device, software fallback, decoder/parser error, missing/extra/reordered frame or timestamp, any `framemd5` difference, truncated playback, visual defect, wrong connector/GPU, nonzero exit or health/event threshold breach. BLOCKED at runtime—not Engineering Decision Pending—when any configured input, golden reference, device binding, display/operator, storage, package or threshold is absent. The end user records the final verdict.
safety_gate: Verify exact GPU/device capability and fail closed on unsupported MPEG-1 hardware decode or software fallback; never use the DeepSeek encoder command as decode evidence.
Verify immutable input/golden hashes and expected metadata before starting. Never synthesize or silently substitute media.
Constrain all output to the approved scratch/evidence root, validate capacity, process only the approved clip/range and write no production data.
Preserve logs/events under ED-17 principles; no generic log clearing. Keep machine integrity proof separate from physical visual proof.
Stop on decode, frame, timestamp, visual, GPU/driver/Xid, thermal/power, storage or evidence anomaly. Do not auto-retry, reset, reboot or change firmware/configuration.
expected_evidence: Source Key/Variant-tagged configuration approval, input/golden hashes, ffprobe metadata and expected frame/timestamp/pixel-format contract
Exact GPU serial/UUID/BDF, driver/VBIOS, ffmpeg build and hardware decoder/capability/no-fallback logs
Full decode log, exit status, actual `framemd5`, byte-for-byte golden comparison and complete frame/timestamp accounting
Time-correlated connector/display/mode identity, physical photos/video or approved captures and qualified operator checklist covering the entire clip
Bounded scratch/capacity proof, preserved pre/during/post GPU/thermal/power/Xid/OS/BMC events, no-retry audit, final state and user verdict
test_case.recovery: Stop the approved player/decoder on the first failure, preserve input, manifests, actual outputs, visual evidence and events, and do not retry. Remove only explicitly approved temporary scratch after evidence retention; restore only the approved display/session state without reset, reboot or firmware action. If GPU/driver/display health remains abnormal, isolate the workload and escalate under the project recovery plan.
